about: Every semantic rule of the det-port Java runtime (gitgalaxy/tools/cobol_to_java/det/cobolrt, #4711): a stable ID, the IBM reference it implements, the options it depends on (#4704), its oracle-assumptions register entries (docs/language_status/register/) and its calibration (#4702). Each rule's code site carries `[rule ID]`; tests/cobol_mainframe/test_cobolrt_rules.py checks both directions.

Status, against IBM (the reference; GnuCOBOL is the instrument): MATCHED -- the runtime implements IBM's documented rule; DIFFERS -- it follows the oracle where z/OS differs or where IBM documents no result and the oracle's answer is modelled (declared in the register); ASSUMED -- IBM leaves it open or the runtime's reading of IBM is not yet confirmed, the choice named; REFUSED -- the runtime stops by name. Calibration: uncalibrated until a z/OS measurement backs the rule (#4702).

JSON GENERATE from a group of DISPLAY, COMP / COMP-3 / COMP-5 / COMP-1 items and fixed tables (an array per table), CONVERTING ... TO JSON BOOLEAN (true on a match, else false): names as written, members in storage order, trailing blanks trimmed, numbers as edited, bytes written to the receiver and counted; a receiver too small is the exception condition under ON EXCEPTION (else a Hole), SUPPRESS ... WHEN / EVERY leaves out an item whose value is ZERO / SPACE / LOW-VALUE / HIGH-VALUE, non-digit numeric data is a Hole (the oracle has no JSON statement)
rules.ibm_note: IBM (Enterprise COBOL 6.4 Language Reference SC27-8713-03, JSON GENERATE statement, Operation of JSON GENERATE, Format conversion of elementary data, Trimming of generated JSON data; Programming Guide SC27-8714-03, Appendix D, Table 109). MATCHED parts: names "exact mixed-case spelling of data-names"; trailing spaces trimmed and "If a character value consists solely of spaces, one space remains"; fixed-point numbers "converted as if they were moved to a numeric-edited item" with "leading zeroes ... up to but not including the digit immediately before the actual or implied decimal point are eliminated. Trailing zeroes after a decimal point are retained" (0000 -> 0, -012.340 -> -12.340); COMP-1 as "an external floating-point data item with PICTURE -9.9(8)E+99"; "A table item that has zero element occurrences is included in the JSON text as an empty array"; SUPPRESS group and ZERO / SPACE / LOW-VALUE / HIGH-VALUE selection and "{\"identifier-2\":{}}"; " is escaped as \" and \ as \\, with \b \t \n \f \r and \uhhhh for the rest of NX'0000'-NX'001F'; "If the receiving area ... is not large enough ... an exception condition exists" and Table 109 code 1. DIFFERS (not declared in the register, so the rule stays ASSUMED): Table 109 code 1 says "The COUNT IN data item, if specified, contains the count of character positions that were actually generated" and the ON EXCEPTION text says the same, while tryGenerate leaves COUNT IN unchanged (X76 says IBM leaves it undefined: it does not). Still ASSUMED because IBM leaves it open: a negative zero, COMP-1 zero (the trimming of 0.00000000E+00 is not stated), the hex-digit case of \uhhhh, and the bytes past the text on an exception ("the content of the receiver ... is undefined"). Declared in X76

rules.title: JSON PARSE INTO a group of DISPLAY, COMP, COMP-3 and COMP-5 items: members matched by name (case-sensitive), strings left-justified and blank padded, numbers stored by decimal alignment; malformed text, a mistyped or non-fitting value is the exception condition under ON EXCEPTION (else a Hole); non-ASCII text, a repeated name, extra decimals, a negative for an unsigned item and an exponent are a Hole (the oracle has no JSON statement)
rules.ibm_note: IBM (Enterprise COBOL 6.4 Language Reference SC27-8713-03, JSON PARSE statement, Operation of JSON PARSE, Table 46; Programming Guide SC27-8714-03, Appendix D, Tables 110 and 111). MATCHED parts: "The JSON text must be valid. Otherwise the statement terminates with an exception condition" (100, 101, 102); superfluous pairs "are tolerated" (JSON-STATUS 2); "If there are no matching items, the statement terminates with an exception condition, and identifier-2 is unmodified" (106); a NAME phrase literal "must match the JSON name exactly in a case sensitive match"; "identifier-2 might be partially modified"; 104 for an incompatible value; 128 and 256 are nonexception, "modified anyway". DIFFERS (not declared in the register, so the rule stays ASSUMED; each needs its own code PR): (a) IBM: "the name-matching between JSON names and COBOL data names is case insensitive" (a-z equals A-Z), the example matches {"g": {"H": {"A": ...}}} to G / h / a; the runtime matches data names case-sensitively (JsonParse.Group.fill uses String.equals) and the rule title says case-sensitive. (b) IBM's own examples wrap the text in the receiving group's name ({"GRP":{...}} INTO GRP) and "the level (qualification) must match" (an omitted level is an exception, 106); the runtime reads the text as the members of the group with no wrapper. (c) Table 46: a JSON string "must consist only of decimal digits" to a numeric item is YES and an integer number to an alphanumeric item is YES; both raise 104 in the runtime. Runtime refusals where IBM states a result (Holes, not guesses): null ("skip assignment", JSON-STATUS 32), an array longer or shorter than its table (8 / 16), a repeated name (4 or 103), true / false (105 / 107), an exponent, more decimals than the item, a negative for an unsigned item. Still ASSUMED because IBM leaves it open: the stored form of a SIZE ERROR number or an over-long string, whether a failing parse leaves earlier items stored, and whether JSON-STATUS is reset per statement. Declared in X77

rules.title: DIVIDE ... REMAINDER: dividend less divisor times the quotient truncated to the first GIVING receiver's scale (not to its high-order digits); a NaN quotient leaves the remainder receiver unchanged
rules.ibm_note: IBM (Enterprise COBOL 6.4 Language Reference SC27-8713-03, DIVIDE statement): "The result of subtracting the product of the quotient and the divisor from the dividend is stored in identifier-4"; "the quotient used to calculate the remainder is in an intermediate field. The value of the intermediate field is truncated rather than rounded"; on a size error in the quotient "the contents of the quotient field (identifier-3) and the remainder field (identifier-4) are unchanged". The remainder formula, truncation and the unchanged receivers match; IBM does not say how many decimal places that intermediate field has, so truncation to the first GIVING receiver's scale (and not its high-order digits) stays the assumption. Declared in C14

ibm.section: MOVE statement: Elementary move rules, numeric receiver

rules.ibm_note: IBM (Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference, SC27-8713-03, MOVE statement, "Elementary move rules", receiver "Numeric or numeric-edited"): "When the category of the sending item is alphanumeric, alphanumeric-edited, national, or national-edited, the data is moved as if the sending item were described as an unsigned integer." Usage note 2: "If the receiving item is numeric and the sending field is an alphanumeric literal, a national literal, or an ALL literal, all characters of the literal must be numeric characters." IBM so defines only digit characters, aligned as an unsigned integer. It states no result for a sign, a decimal point, a space, a comma or a letter in an alphanumeric data item: the runtime's reading of those (a sign and one point read, spaces and the separator skipped, a stray character making the receiver zero, a packed or binary receiver reading the whole text) is libcob's, chosen because IBM leaves it open, so the rule stays ASSUMED. The digits-only case is IBM's. Checked against the 6.4 Language Reference text copy

rules.title: Nonnumeric operands compared byte by byte, the shorter padded with spaces, in the data's byte order or under the PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE's alphabet (ASCII data on the oracle, EBCDIC on z/OS)
A numeric item against a nonnumeric one is its digits as characters (as if moved to an alphanumeric item of as many characters), the sign dropped
Numeric operands compared by value, whatever their usage and the collating sequence
A comparison with a floating-point comparand is made in floating point: a fixed-point item converted to long HFP
An item against an ALL literal: the literal repeated or cut to the item's length, then compared byte by byte
An item against a figurative constant: the constant's character repeated to the item's length (ZERO against a numeric item: by value)

IS NUMERIC: zoned digits with a valid overpunch at the sign position, packed digit nibbles with a valid sign nibble, alphanumeric all digits; under NUMPROC(PFD) a signed item with an F sign is refused
IS ALPHABETIC / ALPHABETIC-UPPER / ALPHABETIC-LOWER: letters and spaces only
DISPLAY of an operand: a signed zoned item as its bytes, a binary or packed item as zoned digits of its PICTURE (signed: the last digit overpunched), any other item as its bytes
STRING ... DELIMITED BY ... INTO ... [WITH POINTER]: bytes transferred in order, the receiver not padded; OVERFLOW when the pointer is outside the receiver or the data does not fit

UNSTRING ... DELIMITED BY ... INTO ... [DELIMITER IN] [COUNT IN] [WITH POINTER] [TALLYING]: the rest to the first INTO with no delimiter; OVERFLOW when the pointer is outside the source or characters remain
INSPECT TALLYING / REPLACING / CONVERTING with BEFORE / AFTER: the phrases act on the original text, the earlier clause takes the characters, TALLYING and REPLACING are separate passes
A LINK's COMMAREA is the caller's storage from the area's first byte, up to the end of the caller's record; bytes past it are LOW-VALUES here (z/OS shows whatever storage follows)
INITIALIZE REPLACING of a table leaves the categories it does not name as they are (IBM); the port stops by name when the occurrences differ, because the oracle copies the first over the others
A COMP / COMP-4 / BINARY item under TRUNC(STD) holds at most its PICTURE's digits (high-order ones lost); under TRUNC(BIN), and a COMP-5 item always, whatever its 2 / 4 / 8 bytes hold
TRUNC(OPT): results as TRUNC(STD), and a value stored past a binary receiver's PICTURE stops by name (IBM: the result is unpredictable)
ARITH(EXTEND): an intermediate result past 30 digits stops by name (GnuCOBOL caps none; IBM's EXTEND range is not modelled)
NUMPROC(PFD): a zoned or packed value read with a sign that is not preferred (C / D signed, F unsigned) is refused by name

Whether a value fits its receiver without losing high-order digits: the PICTURE's digits, or the bytes' range for a binary item under TRUNC(BIN) and COMP-5 (the size error test)

rules.ibm_note: IBM documents no result for non-digit data in a numeric item; the oracle's (GnuCOBOL 3.1.2) rule is modelled

rules.title: Refused by name: a non-digit in a P-scaled item read as an operand or comparand, in an arithmetic receiver, or across 19 or more digits

rules.title: COMP-1 / COMP-2 are HFP: sign bit, excess-64 characteristic (a power of 16), 6 / 14 hexadecimal fraction digits, big-endian; true zero all zero bytes; an unnormalized fraction reads as its value
An exponent overflow (past 16**63) or underflow (below 16**-65) is refused by name: z/OS's answer depends on the program mask and Language Environment
ADD / SUBTRACT: the operands aligned with one hexadecimal guard digit, the sum normalized and truncated
MULTIPLY: the exact product truncated to the precision
DIVIDE: the exact quotient truncated to the precision
A zero divisor: as a statement's whole value, libcob's NaN with the size error raised (the receiver unchanged); inside a larger expression refused by name
rules.ibm_note: z/OS leaves a zero divisor's result undefined; the oracle's NaN is modelled

rules.title: A long value into a COMP-1 is rounded (LOAD ROUNDED: a one added at the first discarded bit)
An IEEE binary32 / binary64 pattern to and from COMP-1 / COMP-2: binary64 exact in long HFP, binary32 truncated to long then rounded to short, HFP to IEEE nearest ties to even
rules.ibm_note: IBM documents no IEEE converter for a COMP-1 / COMP-2 item; the model's choice (det/hfp.py from_ieee / to_ieee). The one documented HFP-IEEE conversion is the Java interop's (Language Reference, the note on COMP-1 / COMP-2 against Java float / double: LE __fp_htob / __fp_btoh, biased round to nearest = ties away from 0): from_ieee agrees with it, to_ieee rounds ties to even and does not (register C6, #8700)

rules.title: A fixed-point value converted to long HFP: the exact value truncated to 14 hexadecimal digits (then rounded to short for a COMP-1)
rules.ibm_note: IBM says only that a fixed-point number is converted to the internal floating-point numbering system, and that up to 15 digits survive a COMP-2 round trip (Programming Guide, 'Conversions and precision'); it does not say truncated or rounded: truncation is the model's choice, consistent with the round trip (register C6, #8700)

rules.title: A floating-point exponentiation: the exact power for an integer exponent, exp(b ln a) at 60 digits for a fractional one, truncated to long HFP
rules.ibm_note: IBM documents long floating-point arithmetic for a floating-point exponentiation and an undefined negative base to a fractional power (Programming Guide, Appendix A, 'Exponentiations evaluated in floating-point arithmetic'), no result digits; the capture kit's reference power() is the model until captured z/OS output agrees

rules.title: A float moved to a fixed-point item: rounded in the receiver's low-order position, at most 9 (COMP-1) / 18 (COMP-2) significant digits
FUNCTION NUMVAL / NUMVAL-C in a floating-point expression: long HFP of the value under ARITH(COMPAT); more than 18 digits, or more than 15 significant ones, refused by name
rules.ibm_note: IBM (Enterprise COBOL 6.4 Programming Guide, SC27-8714-03, "Converting to numbers"): "NUMVAL, NUMVAL-C and NUMVAL-F return long (64-bit) floating-point values in compatibility mode, and return extended-precision (128-bit) floating-point values in extended mode"; "At most 15 decimal digits can be converted accurately to long-precision floating point ... Otherwise, the result may lose precision in an unexpected manner." Language Reference (SC27-8713-03), NUMVAL: "If the ARITH(COMPAT) compiler option is in effect, the total number of digits must not exceed 18." The long result under ARITH(COMPAT), and the 18-digit and 15-digit refusals (where IBM describes no result), MATCH; ARITH(EXTEND) is refused by name. IBM does not say how the decimal digits become the long value (truncated or rounded), which the runtime truncates (register C6, ASSUMED list): stays ASSUMED. Checked against the text copies

A number through a numeric-edited PICTURE: 9, Z / * zero suppression, the . and , insertion characters, fixed + / -, CR / DB, B 0 /, and a zero value of an all-suppression PICTURE
A floating insertion string ($$$,$$9.99, +++9, ---9) floats the sign or currency string to just left of the first significant digit; every digit position in the string and a zero value: all spaces
The currency symbol ($ or the declared PICTURE SYMBOL) stands for the program's CURRENCY SIGN string
A zoned sender holding non-digits: its bytes are the PICTURE's digits as they are, only a '0' suppressed

rules.ibm_note: IBM (Enterprise COBOL 6.4 Language Reference, TEST-NUMVAL): 0 when argument-1 conforms to NUMVAL; else "the position of the first character in error"; otherwise "FUNCTION LENGTH (argument-1) + 1" (zero-length, all spaces, or valid but incomplete such as ' +.'); '0 1' returns 3. rules.title: FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE where the project has no clock bean: YYYYMMDDHHMMSShh and the UTC offset of the run's clock
rules.ibm_note: IBM (Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference, SC27-8713-03, "CURRENT-DATE"): "The CURRENT-DATE function returns a 21-character alphanumeric value that represents the calendar date, time of day, and time differential from Greenwich mean time provided by the system on which the function is evaluated." Positions 1-16 are year, month, day, hours, minutes, seconds and hundredths of a second; position 17: "The character '+' is returned if the local time indicated is the same as or ahead of Greenwich mean time"; positions 18-21 are the hours and minutes of that difference. The runtime's 21 characters (yyyyMMddHHmmss, hundredths, then a fixed +0000) have IBM's layout, and +0000 is IBM's text only when the clock reads Greenwich mean time. The clock's value is the run's, which IBM cannot define; but the runtime writes +0000 whatever zone its clock is in, where IBM reports the actual differential. Stays ASSUMED, the offset a recorded gap, not hidden. Checked against the 6.4 Language Reference text copy

rules.title: PUT CONTAINER FROM FLENGTH(n): the first n bytes (negative: LENGERR RESP2 1); GET CONTAINER INTO FLENGTH: the most the area takes; a FLENGTH past the area refused
rules.ibm_note: IBM (CICS TS 6 API Reference, PUT CONTAINER (CHANNEL), GET CONTAINER (CHANNEL), local manual text). MATCHED: a GET CONTAINER INTO shorter than the container is truncated with LENGERR; PUT CONTAINER "RESP2 1: A negative number was specified on the FLENGTH option". rules.title: START FROM(f) LENGTH(n): the first n bytes, LENGERR when LENGTH is not greater than zero; past FROM refused
RETRIEVE RTRANSID / RTERMID / QUEUE: the value MOVEd into the program's area, padded with spaces or truncated; RETRIEVE INTO the bytes
rules.ibm_note: IBM (CICS TS 6 API Reference, RETRIEVE, INTO and LENGTH, local manual text). The area sizes and LENGTH are quoted in X18. Padding a shorter START data value with spaces in INTO is the runtime's reading; IBM does not state what INTO holds past the data. Stays ASSUMED. No DIFFERS is claimed. Declared in X18

rules.title: READ INTO LENGTH(max): the record truncated to max, LENGERR (RESP2 11) when longer, the rest of INTO as it was; a negative LENGTH or a record past INTO refused
rules.ibm_note: IBM (CICS TS 6 API Reference, READ, INTO and LENGTH, local manual text). MATCHED: a record longer than the area is truncated, LENGERR RESP 22 RESP2 11 is raised, and LENGTH is set to the record's length. IBM calls the remainder of INTO after a shorter record unpredictable, so the runtime's choice stays ASSUMED. Possible DIFFERS, not settled: LENGERR for a fixed-length file read into a longer area; IBM's text was not read to a conclusion, so the rule stays ASSUMED. Declared in X14

rules.title: READQ TD INTO: the record (cut to LENGTH) goes INTO, the rest of INTO as it was; a record moved past INTO refused
rules.ibm_note: IBM (CICS TS 6 API Reference, READQ TD, INTO and LENGTH, local manual text). MATCHED: a record longer than the area is truncated to LENGTH and LENGTH is set to the record's length (LENGERR). Still ASSUMED because IBM leaves it open: the bytes of INTO past a shorter record (the runtime leaves them unchanged), and a negative or zero LENGTH. No DIFFERS is claimed. Declared in X6, X57

rules.title: BIF DEEDIT: the characters other than the digits removed, the digits right-aligned and zero-padded, a trailing sign kept as the last digit's zone
rules.ibm_note: IBM keeps the rightmost byte unaltered only when its zone is X'A'-X'F' AND its numeric portion is X'0'-X'9'; the runtime tests the zone alone, so a trailing '[' or ']' (X'BA' / X'BB' in CCSID 037) is kept where IBM removes it. Same on the stub (GGCDEED); declared in X26

rules.title: TS items are in the region's code page (the estate's EBCDIC page, else CCSID 037): the program's bytes moved byte for byte, a byte with no character in both pages stops the run by name
rules.ibm_note: IBM (CICS TS for z/OS 6, API Reference, ASSIGN, LOCALCCSID): "This option returns the fullword binary Coded Character Set Identifier (CCSID) used for the CICS region. It is the value specified on the LOCALCCSID system initialization parameter." Application Programming, Chapter 5 (containers): "If the application programmer does not specify a code page for data conversion, CICS uses the default code page for the whole of the local CICS region, which is specified on the LOCALCCSID system initialization parameter"; "the message data is taken to be in the region's EBCDIC code page". MATCHED in part: the region has one code page, set by the installation, and EBCDIC is its default. Still ASSUMED because IBM states no rule for temporary storage items (the WRITEQ TS pages say nothing of a code page: TS data is the program's own bytes) or for a byte with no character in both pages: the runtime moving the program's bytes unconverted into the region's page, with an unmapped byte stopping the run by name, is our choice. Declared in C18

rules.title: ASSIGN of a short value (SYSID: 4 bytes) into a longer area: the first bytes, the rest as it was
rules.ibm_note: IBM (CICS TS 6 API Reference, ASSIGN, local manual text). MATCHED: the option values ASSIGN returns. DIFFERS (not declared in the register, so the rule stays ASSUMED): after an INVREQ IBM says the other options are still populated, while cics_conditions.assign and the stub write nothing to the data areas. Declared in X19

rules.title: A symbolic map field's subfields: attribute, colour and highlight bytes (recorded as they are: X'00' and the space X'40' are values), length -1 the cursor; RECEIVE MAP's input text padded and its length without trailing blanks
rules.ibm_note: IBM (Developing CICS Applications, SEND MAP) treats an attribute byte as not present only when it is X'00' or a leftover of an input operation (X'80', X'02', X'82'), and an extended attribute byte only when null; the runtime records every byte as it is (#7955: X'00' and a space are values the harness compares), so a space attribute (X'40') is recorded where IBM sends it, and a leftover X'80' / X'02' / X'82' is set where IBM ignores it. RECEIVE's <f>L is the characters the terminal sent (blanks keyed included), the runtime's the text without trailing blanks. Declared in X2

rules.title: RECEIVE MAP into a DFHMDF JUSTIFY=(LEFT|RIGHT[,BLANK|ZERO]) field: the typed text placed at the justified end, the rest filled with blanks or zeros; <f>L the length typed
rules.ibm_note: IBM's DFHMDF JUSTIFY table assumes the missing half: LEFT gives BLANK, RIGHT gives ZERO, BLANK gives LEFT, ZERO gives RIGHT. The runtime fills with ZERO only when ZERO is coded and places RIGHT only when RIGHT is coded, so JUSTIFY=(RIGHT) fills with blanks (IBM: zeros) and JUSTIFY=(,ZERO) is left-justified (IBM: right). Declared in X54

rules.title: FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE in a CICS task: the task's clock, the region's zone (UTC)
rules.ibm_note: IBM (Enterprise COBOL 6.4 Language Reference SC27-8713-03, CURRENT-DATE). MATCHED: the 21-character layout, the hundredths in positions 15-16, and "The character '+' is returned if the local time indicated is the same as or ahead of Greenwich mean time" with a zero differential (+0000). Still ASSUMED: which clock a CICS task reads; IBM says "the system on which the function is evaluated" and gives no CICS region zone, so the task's clock at UTC is the choice. No DIFFERS is claimed. Declared in X4

rules.title: The RESP value of each condition, and the condition of each value (DFHRESP)
A condition with no HANDLE CONDITION label abends, except those IBM's default action ignores (EOC)

RECEIVE INTO: the data into the first bytes of the area, the rest as it was; RECEIVE SET: the data copied into the record, a byte past it X'00'
rules.ibm_note: IBM (CICS TS 6 API Reference, RECEIVE, LENGTH, MAXLENGTH, NOTRUNCATE and SET, local manual text). MATCHED: the LENGTH, MAXLENGTH and NOTRUNCATE behaviour and the length returned with SET. The rule's remaining choices are not stated by IBM and stay ASSUMED. No DIFFERS is claimed. Declared in X15

rules.title: GETMAIN SET (INITIMG, LENGERR RESP2 1 sets the pointer to zero), WEB RECEIVE SET, SET ADDRESS OF / SET pointer TO ADDRESS OF: handles to blocks of task storage, a record and its block one storage
rules.ibm_note: IBM (CICS TS 6 API Reference, GETMAIN, local manual text). MATCHED: "Sets the pointer reference to the address of the acquired main storage"; "A LENGERR condition that results from a zero or negative value that is specified for FLENGTH or LENGTH sets ptr-ref to zero"; "There is no default initialization"; INITIMG: "CICS sets every byte". Still ASSUMED: the pointer as an 8-byte handle of a block of task storage (IBM defines an address; z/OS storage is not modelled), and the SET ADDRESS OF methods, which no CICS page covers. The FREEMAIN INVREQ and WEB RECEIVE SET text were not read here. No DIFFERS is claimed. Declared in X47

rules.title: ADDRESS COMMAREA(ptr): the handle of the DFHCOMMAREA record's bytes; a task with no COMMAREA is refused (IBM's X'FF000000' is no COBOL NULL), except in a program with no 01 DFHCOMMAREA, where it is the X'FF000000' handle the byte-view test reads (addressNoCommarea); a COMMAREA there is refused; ADDRESS TWA / TCTUA / CWA(ptr): the handle of the task's work area / the terminal's user area / the region's common work area, X'FF000000' when its size is 0 or unstated (addressTwa, addressTctua, addressCwa; reachable from a program: the spec models them, sized by the definitions)
rules.ibm_note: IBM (CICS TS 6 API Reference, ADDRESS, local manual text). MATCHED: "If the COMMAREA does not exist, the pointer reference is set to the null value, X'FF000000'"; the same for CWA, TCTUA and TWA. The runtime matches for CWA, TWA and TCTUA. For COMMAREA it refuses a task with no COMMAREA, a named refusal and not an IBM difference, so it stays ASSUMED. Declared in X59

rules.title: SET(ptr) of RECEIVE, RETRIEVE, READQ TS, GET CONTAINER, READ, READNEXT and READPREV: a new block of task storage holding the data, its handle in the pointer, valid until the command IBM names ends it
rules.ibm_note: IBM (CICS TS 6 API Reference, READ, READNEXT / READPREV, READQ TS, RETRIEVE, RECEIVE, GET CONTAINER (CHANNEL), local manual text). MATCHED: each lifetime the rule names (READ "until the next READ command for the same file or until completion of a corresponding REWRITE, DELETE, or UNLOCK command, or a SYNCPOINT in the case of READ UPDATE SET"; READNEXT "no longer valid after an ENDBR or SYNCPOINT"; READQ TS "until the next READQ TS command or the end of task"; RECEIVE "until the next receive command or the end of task"; GET CONTAINER until the next GET with SET, DELETE, MOVE, end of channel scope or DELETE CHANNEL). Still ASSUMED: the new block of task storage per command (IBM says CICS supplies a buffer and does not say what it holds afterwards), and RETRIEVE, where IBM states no end for the pointer. No DIFFERS is claimed. Declared in X58

rules.title: OS/VS COBOL chained storage areas: an address moved between a BLL cell and a fullword of data is a token both runtimes number alike (0 NULL, the n-th address n * 65536; a value no cell gave is refused), and a record is addressed again through its cell at a paragraph name (a null cell leaves it as it is)
rules.ibm_note: CICS/MVS 2.1.2 Application Programmer's Reference SC33-0512-1, 'BLL and chained storage areas' (p. 22): not an online IBM doc; the token is assumed (a real address does not fit a fullword in the instrument)

rules.title: A planned SQL fault (PROGRAM LINE NTH SQLCODE SQLSTATE) replaces the statement's execution, the SQLCA set as Db2 would set it
rules.ibm_note: the faults are the harness's; the SQLCA a fault leaves is assumed

rules.title: The SQLCA a statement leaves: SQLCODE 0 and no warning before its outcome, then Db2's SQLCODE, SQLSTATE, SQLERRM tokens, SQLERRP, SQLERRD and warnings (IBM's driver's own SQLCA where it has one)

ibm.section: Appendix F. SQL communication area (SQLCA), Description of SQLCA fields (Table 262)

rules.ibm_note: IBM (Db2 13 for z/OS SQL Reference, Appendix F, "Description of SQLCA fields", Table 262): "An SQLCA is a structure or collection of variables that is updated after each SQL statement executes." SQLCAID: "containing the text 'SQLCA'"; SQLCABC: "Contains the length of the SQLCA: 136"; SQLCODE: 0 "Successful execution (though there might have been warning messages)", positive "Successful execution, but with a warning condition or other information", negative "Error condition"; SQLERRMC: "one or more tokens, separated by X'FF'"; SQLERRP: "In all cases, the first three characters are 'DSN' for Db2 for z/OS"; SQLERRD(3): the number of rows that qualified for a DELETE, INSERT, UPDATE or MERGE, "The value is 0 if the SQL statement fails"; SQLWARN0: "a W if at least one other indicator contains a W or Z". The runtime's reset (SQLCAID 'SQLCA', 136, SQLCODE 0, SQLSTATE 00000, no warning) and the sign of SQLCODE follow that text. Not IBM's: SQLERRP is left blank by a statement that succeeds and is the Db2 for LUW driver's after an error, where IBM says it starts 'DSN' in all cases (register Q1 declares the oracle's engine is not z/OS), and the SQLERRMC, SQLERRD and SQLSTATE values after an error are the oracle engine's, which IBM defines for z/OS only: stays ASSUMED. Checked against the Db2 13 SQL Reference text copy

rules.title: Host variables in: PIC X(n) as CHAR(n) (trailing blanks kept), a 49-level pair as VARCHAR, a numeric item as DECIMAL / SMALLINT / INTEGER / BIGINT, NULL when the indicator is negative

ibm.section: Equivalent SQL and COBOL data types

rules.title: A searched UPDATE / DELETE (or INSERT ... SELECT) that changes no row is SQLCODE +100
SELECT INTO: the one row; no row +100, more than one -811

A row into host variables: a string padded or truncated (SQLWARN0 / SQLWARN1 'W', the indicator the original length), a number whose integer part does not fit -304 and nothing assigned, NULL without an indicator -305

COMMIT: the unit of work committed, cursors not WITH HOLD closed; ROLLBACK: backed out, every cursor closed; refused with no unit of work; in a CICS program COMMIT answers -925 and ROLLBACK -926 (SQLSTATE 2D521; Db2 for z/OS Codes) and ends nothing
SAVEPOINT / ROLLBACK TO / RELEASE SAVEPOINT as written, on the unit's connection (-880: no such savepoint), set ON ROLLBACK RETAIN CURSORS
OPEN (-502 when open; WITH HOLD survives COMMIT), FETCH (+100 at the end, -501 when not open), CLOSE (-501 when not open); a task's or step's end closes its cursors

FETCH PRIOR / FIRST / LAST / CURRENT / ABSOLUTE n / RELATIVE n of an insensitive SCROLL cursor: a position over the rows read at OPEN (a move off either end is +100 and clamps; FETCH CURRENT with no current row is refused: +231 on z/OS, +100 on LUW)
FETCH BEFORE / AFTER of an insensitive SCROLL cursor: parks it before the first row or after the last, SQLCODE 0, no row and no host variable touched

FETCH [NEXT] ROWSET FROM cursor FOR n ROWS INTO host-variable tables: up to n next rows, one table per column, SQLERRD(3) the rows read; a rowset that reaches the end holds fewer than n rows and is +100 (an n above the tables is refused)

INSERT ... VALUES (host-variable tables) FOR n ROWS [ATOMIC]: the single-row INSERT for elements 1..n, SQLERRD(3) the rows inserted; a first row that fails is Db2's error, a later one is refused (ATOMIC's undo is not modelled)
UPDATE / DELETE WHERE CURRENT OF: the current row (-501 not open, -508 no current row)
The 12-byte feedback code: all zero for success, else severity 3, the message number, case / severity / control and 'CEE'; what the model does not model refused by name
Lilian day 1 is 15 October 1582 (Gregorian leap years); Lilian second 86400 is 00:00:00 on that day; a seconds item travels by value in its own usage (COMP-2: HFP on z/OS)
Picture strings: the date / time terms LE documents, formatted and parsed; any other term refused by name

ibm.section: Picture character terms and picture strings

rules.title: A VSTRING result: halfword length then the text, the rest of the item untouched

ibm.section: Data type definitions: VSTRING (COBOL: STRING-OUT PIC X(80)); CEEDATE / CEEDATM output_char_date

rules.ibm_note: IBM (z/OS 3.1 Language Environment Programming Reference, SA38-0683-60, "Data type definitions" table for COBOL, VSTRING): "A halfword length-prefixed character string (for input); fixed-length 80-character string (for output)", declared "01 STRING-IN. 02 LEN PIC S9(4) USAGE IS BINARY. 02 TXT PIC X(N)." for input and "01 STRING-OUT PIC X(80)." for output. CEEDATE: output_char_date is "A fixed-length 80-character string (VSTRING)" and, "If input_Lilian_date is not valid, output_char_date is set to all blanks." Input VSTRINGs (the picture) are halfword-prefixed, as the runtime reads them. For an OUTPUT, IBM documents a plain 80-byte text with no length prefix and blanks on error; the runtime writes a halfword length then the text, leaves the rest of the item untouched and, on error, writes a zero length (register L6 assumption 2, which says IBM states no COBOL layout: this text does). That is a difference, not an open point; it is kept ASSUMED here and filed as a bug in #8700 (both sides of the harness share the prefixed model, so no case sees it). Checked against the LE Programming Reference text copy

rules.title: CEEGMT / CEEUTC: the run's clock is GMT; Lilian day and seconds

ibm.section: CEEGMT: get current Greenwich Mean Time (CEEUTC alias)

rules.ibm_note: IBM (z/OS 3.1 Language Environment Programming Reference, SA38-0683-60, "CEEGMT"): "CEEGMT returns the current Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) as both a Lilian date and as the number of seconds since 00:00:00 14 October 1582." "In order for the results of this service to be meaningful, your system's TOD (time-of-day) clock must be set to Greenwich Mean Time and be based on the standard epoch." output_GMT_Lilian: a 32-bit binary integer, "the number of days since 14 October 1582 (16 May 1988 is day number 148138)"; output_GMT_seconds: a 64-bit double floating-point number, "the number of seconds since 00:00:00 on 14 October 1582, not counting leap seconds" ("00:00:01 on 15 October 1582 is second number 86,401"); fc CEE000 on success; "Language Environment treats Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) and Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) as the same. You can use the CEEUTC service, which is an alias of the CEEGMT service". The runtime does what this says: its clock is GMT, the day count and the seconds (with the clock's hundredths) are IBM's, a fullword and a COMP-2, success feedback zero, CEEUTC the same method. IBM's one failure, CEE2E6 (GMT not available, outputs 0), cannot arise from a pinned clock and is not modelled (an unpinned clock is refused by name, L6). The clock's value is the run's, which IBM cannot define. Checked against the LE Programming Reference text copy

rules.title: CEEGMTO / CEEUTCO: the offset from GMT is zero on the GMT clock

ibm.section: CEEGMTO: get offset from Greenwich Mean Time to local time

rules.ibm_note: IBM (z/OS 3.1 Language Environment Programming Reference, SA38-0683-60, "CEEGMTO"): "CEEGMTO returns values to the calling routine representing the difference between the local system time and Greenwich Mean Time (GMT)." offset_hours: "the offset from GMT to local time, in hours. For example, for Pacific Standard Time, offset_hours equals -8"; offset_minutes "0 to 59"; offset_seconds: "-28,800 (-8 * 60 * 60)" for Pacific standard time; "If local time offset is not available, offset_hours equals 0 and CEEGMTO terminates with a non-CEE000" code (CEE2E7, message 2503). IBM defines the output as the real difference of the system's local time from GMT. The runtime answers 0, 0, 0.0 and success whatever zone the system is in, because its clock is read as GMT (register L6 assumption 1): that equals IBM only when the local zone is GMT, and no zone is modelled. Stays ASSUMED, the zone gap recorded, as for CURRENT-DATE's +0000. Checked against the LE Programming Reference text copy

rules.title: DSNTIAC: formats an SQLCA into message lines (a stand-in; the text is unproven)

ibm.section: Displaying SQLCA fields by calling DSNTIAR; DSNTIAC (assembler and COBOL syntax)

rules.ibm_note: IBM (Db2 13 for z/OS Application Programming and SQL Guide, "Displaying SQLCA fields by calling DSNTIAR" and "DSNTIAC"): "If your CICS application requires CICS storage handling, you must use the subroutine DSNTIAC instead of DSNTIAR", called "CALL 'DSNTIAC' USING eib commarea sqlca msg lrecl"; "Both DSNTIAC and DSNTIAR format the SQLCA in the same way." The message area is a halfword total length ("the minimum length of the output area is 240-bytes") then lines of lrecl, lrecl "in the range 72-240 bytes"; "DSNTIAR places up to 10 lines in the message area. If the text of a message is longer than the record length you specify on DSNTIAR, the output message splits into several records, on word boundaries if possible. The split records are indented. All records begin with a blank character for carriage control. If you have more lines than the message output area can contain, DSNTIAR issues a return code of 4. A completely blank record marks the end of the message output area." Return codes: 0 successful; 4 more data than fit; 8 "Logical record length not in the range 72-240, inclusive"; 12 "Message area not large enough. The message length was 240 or greater."; 16 TSO message routine error; 20 DSNTIA1 not loaded; 24 "SQLCA data error". The runtime's return codes 0, 4, 8, 12 (no whole line in the area) and 24 and its line length range are IBM's. The text is Db2's message catalogue (IBM gives no byte-for-byte text, register Q5), and three layout points differ from the quote: the runtime's lines do not begin with a carriage-control blank, its split lines are not indented, and it does not cap the text at 10 lines. Filed as a bug in #8700; the rule stays ASSUMED, not matched. Checked against the Db2 13 Application Programming and SQL Guide text copy

rules.title: ZUIDSTCK: the 16 TOD bytes are a stated input of the run, opaque to the program (a stand-in; never the host clock)
rules.ibm_note: IBM (z/Architecture Principles of Operation, SA22-7832, "STORE CLOCK EXTENDED", STCKE): "the following are stored into the 16-byte second operand: ... the epoch index is stored in byte position 0 [when the multiple-epoch facility is installed]. The current value of the TOD clock is stored in byte positions 1-13. The TOD programmable field, bits 16-31 of the TOD programmable register, is stored in byte positions 14 and 15." "Zeros are stored at the operand location when the clock is in the error state or the not-operational state." ZUIDSTCK is not an IBM service: it is zECS's own assembler wrapper around STCKE, so IBM defines only the 16-byte layout it wraps. The runtime makes the 16 bytes a stated input of the run and never the host clock (register X47): the layout is IBM's, the value is the machine's, which no manual states. The program keeps only bytes 1-6 (epoch index and the first five clock bytes) as a key prefix. IBM neither confirms nor contradicts the stand-in, so the rule stays ASSUMED. Checked against the z/Architecture Principles of Operation text copy

rules.title: CEEQCEN / CEESCEN: the century window's start (80 by default; CEESCEN sets 0 to 100, else CEE2533)

ibm.section: CEEQCEN: query the century window; CEESCEN: set the century window

rules.ibm_note: IBM (z/OS 3.1 Language Environment Programming Reference, SA38-0683-60, "CEEQCEN" and "CEESCEN"): century_start is "An integer between 0 and 100 indicating the year on which the century window is based. For example, if the Language Environment default is in effect, all 2-digit years lie within the 100-year window starting 80 years prior to the system date. CEEQCEN then returns the value 80." CEESCEN: "An integer between 0 and 100, setting the century window." The runtime's default 80, its 0-to-100 range and a CEEQCEN that returns what CEESCEN set are IBM's. What IBM leaves open: the reaction to a value outside 0-100 (the runtime answers CEE2533 and keeps the setting; this manual lists no such code for CEESCEN, only CEE000 and CEE2E6, the latter being the GMT message), and the scope ("Century intervals are kept as thread-level data" against "CEESCEN applies to the enclave"; the runtime holds one setting for the run). Stays ASSUMED. Checked against the LE Programming Reference text copy

ibm.section: CEELOCT: get current local date or time

rules.ibm_note: IBM (z/OS 3.1 Language Environment Programming Reference, SA38-0683-60, "CEELOCT"): "CEELOCT returns the current local date or time in three formats: Lilian date, Lilian seconds, Gregorian character string (in the form YYYYMMDDHHMISS999)"; output_Lilian a 32-bit binary integer ("day 1 equals 15 October 1582, day 148,887 equals 4 June 1990"); output_seconds a 64-bit double floating-point number ("19:00:01.078 on 4 June 1990 is second number 12,863,905,201.078"); output_Gregorian "A 17-byte fixed-length character string in the form YYYYMMDDHHMISS999"; fc CEE000, or CEE2F3 (severity 3, message 2531, "The local time was not available from the system"). The runtime's three outputs, the 17 bytes (register L5 assumption 3, the longer field, is not what IBM documents), the success feedback and the CEE2F3 token are IBM's. One difference: for CEE2F3 IBM says "output_Lilian is set to 0" and "output_seconds is set to 0"; the planned-fault path (Ceeloct.fail) leaves the outputs as they were. Filed as a bug in #8700, so the rule is not MATCHED. The clock is the run's (the zone is the pinned clock's, L5 assumption 1). Checked against the LE Programming Reference text copy

rules.title: COBDATFT (CardDemo's assembler date routine): input type '2' to output type '2' modelled byte for byte; type '1' and the error path depend on the load module's literal pool: refused
MVSWAIT (CardDemo's assembler wait routine): returns at once with RETURN-CODE 0, caller storage untouched (the timer wait is not observable); an argument shorter than the fullword it loads: refused
ENTRY 'DLITCBL': each DB PCB of the PSB bound to the area IMS passes, its mask filled (DBD name, level 00, blank status, PROCOPT, sensitive segments, key feedback zero)

The stated database: DBD / PSB configuration and seed loaded in hierarchic sequence (refused when out of order), new twins placed by segment type and sequence field, each database written at the step's end
rules.ibm_note: IBM (IMS 15.4 Application Programming, "Sequential access"; IMS 15.4 Application Programming APIs, DBD AMBIGUOUS INSERT): "When you use a sequential access method, the segments in the database are stored in hierarchic sequence, one after another"; a unique sequence field fixes the twin order; for FIRST / LAST / HERE the DBD's insert rule applies only to a segment "with no sequence field or with a nonunique sequence field" and "The value is ignored when specified for a segment type with a unique sequence field". The runtime stores twins by segment type and sequence field, which is IBM's order. IBM says nothing about how a harness loads a database: refusing an out-of-order seed and the DBD / PSB configuration reader are the harness's own (registers I1, I6), so the rule stays ASSUMED. Checked against the IMS 15.4 text copies

rules.title: SSAs: segment name, unqualified (blank) or qualified (field, relational operator, value, ')'); qualification statements joined by AND (& or *) and OR (+ or |), AND binding tighter, at most 16; AC / AJ / AK as IBM answers them; command codes F, L, P, C, D and - (L only on the last unqualified SSA of a GU, P only on a GU, C only as the one SSA of a GU, D on a get call), the other codes, the independent AND (#) and missing levels refused
rules.ibm_note: IBM (IMS 15.4 Application Programming, "Multiple qualification statements"; IMS 15.4 Application Programming APIs, "Command codes"; IMS 15.4 Messages and Codes Volume 4 (IMS Component Codes), AC, AJ, AK): AC "The call specifies two SSAs for the same hierarchic level" and "the SSA specifying that segment name is not in its correct hierarchic sequence"; AK "An SSA contains an invalid field name"; AJ "the format of one of the SSAs is invalid"; "Logical AND ... (coded * or &)", "Logical OR ... (coded + or |)", "A set is a number of qualification statements that are joined by an AND ... Each OR starts a new set" (AND binds tighter); the independent AND is "Use it only with secondary indexes" (refused here); the null command code is "Use an SSA in command code format without specifying the command code". Those parts MATCH. Two choices go past IBM and are refusals, not wrong answers: the runtime's limit of 16 qualification statements (MAX_TERMS) where IBM says "You can use a maximum of 1024 qualification statements on a call", and L / P / C refused outside one call shape where IBM's command-code table allows each on every get (C also on ISRT: "You can use the C command code for all Get calls and for the ISRT call"). Stays ASSUMED, the choices named. Checked against the IMS 15.4 text copies

rules.title: A qualification compares the field's stored bytes (C / X); a P field only where packed and logical comparison agree (both valid, one positive sign)
The PCB mask after a call: status code, segment level, segment name, concatenated key and its length
rules.ibm_note: IBM (IMS 15.4 Application Programming, "Specifying the DB PCB mask", Table 35 and notes 2-9): the layout is database name 8, segment level 2, status code 2, processing options 4, reserved 4, segment name 8, length of key feedback area 4 (binary), number of sensitive segments 4 (binary), key feedback area: the runtime's offsets are that order. Note 2: "If IMS is unable to find the segment that you request, it gives you the level number of the last segment it encounters that satisfied your call"; note 9: "IMS does not normally clear the key feedback area. IMS sets this length of the key feedback area to indicate the portion of the area that is valid". Those parts MATCH. IBM is silent on the mask after GB, REPL, DLET and II (the runtime leaves level, name and key as they were, or gives the parent) and on GNP's GE; the entry contents are the runtime's (RT-DLI-ENTRY carries a separate DIFFERS: note 6 puts the database type in SEGNAME at scheduling). Stays ASSUMED (register I4). Checked against the IMS 15.4 text copies

rules.title: GU / GN / GNP and their holds: the first segment in hierarchic sequence satisfying the SSAs, from the database's start, from position, or under parentage; GE / GB / GP / GA / GK; position and parentage after the call; command code D hands back the D-coded segments before the found one

ibm.section: GU / GHU, GN / GHN, GNP / GHNP calls

rules.ibm_note: IBM (IMS 15.4 Application Programming, Chapter 15 "Current position in the database after each call"; IMS 15.4 Application Programming APIs, "GU/GHU call", "GN/GHN call", "GNP/GHNP call", "D command code"): "A GU call with an unqualified SSA at the root level attempts to satisfy the call by starting at the beginning of the database"; GN "Processing moves forward from current position"; GNP: "The search for the requested segment is limited to the dependents of the lowest-level segment most recently accessed by a GU or GN call"; GP and GK as the runtime answers them. D: "The D command code has no effect on the IMS retrieval logic. The only thing it does is cause each segment to be moved to your I/O area", the segments "one after the other, left to right" and "IMS always returns the last segment in the path". Position after a successful call MATCHES. Where IBM answers by IMS's own search (position after a GE from GU, after II, a qualified GN that finds nothing: GE or GB) the runtime refuses the next call that needs it (stricter, never different). Not read against the runtime here: the missing-SSA derivation, and D's P-processing-option requirement. Stays ASSUMED (register I3). Checked against the IMS 15.4 text copies

rules.title: EXEC DLI GU / GN / GNP USING PCB(n) [SEGMENT WHERE] INTO under CICS: the CBLTDLI get of the same SSAs against PCB n of the scheduled PSB, a hold where PROCOPT allows an update; DIBSTAT the PCB's status
rules.ibm_note: IBM (IMS 15.4 Application Programming, "Comparing call-level and command-level programs", note 1 to the table of call and command equivalents): "Get commands are just like Get Hold calls, and the performance of Get commands and Get calls is the same." IMS 15.4 Application Programming APIs, Table 55: "Get commands (GU, GHU, GN, GHN, GNP, GHNP)" are valid in Batch, BMP and CICS with DBCTL; GU command usage: "Use the GU command to retrieve specific segments from the database, or to establish a position in the database for sequential processing"; REPL command: "that segment must already have been defined as replace-sensitive in the PCB by specifying PROCOPT=A or PROCOPT=R" and "You cannot issue any commands using the same PCB between a Get command and the REPL command". So IBM documents the hold (the register I5 premise that the command has no HOLD option and the hold is assumed is settled: every EXEC DLI get is a hold). The runtime holds only where the PCB's PROCOPT allows an update (A, R or D); on any other PCB a REPL / DLET answers AM before the held-segment check (change(), DJ comes after AM), so the held/not-held difference is unobservable. MATCHED. Checked against the IMS 15.4 text copies (release 15.4; the register cited 15.3)

rules.title: EXEC DLI ISRT USING PCB(n) SEGMENT(s) [WHERE ...] ... SEGMENT(t) FROM(area) [SEGLENGTH(n)] under CICS: the CBLTDLI ISRT of the same SSAs against PCB n of the scheduled PSB; segments are fixed length, so a SEGLENGTH that differs from the DBD's stops the run; DIBSTAT the PCB's status
rules.ibm_note: IBM (IMS 15.4 Application Programming APIs, "ISRT command"): "You must include at least a SEGMENT option for each segment you want to add to the database. Unless ISRT is a path command, the lowest level SEGMENT option specifies the segment being inserted. You cannot use a WHERE or KEYS option for this level." (the runtime's last SSA unqualified: MATCHES); SEGLENGTH: "Requirement: The value specified for SEGLENGTH must be greater than or equal to the length of the longest segment that can be processed by this call." The runtime stops by name on any SEGLENGTH that differs from the segment's fixed length, so it refuses a longer one IBM accepts (stricter, never a different result). Missing parent SEGMENT options: IBM takes the current position or the first occurrence; the runtime reads the same rule through the CBLTDLI ISRT (not compared here). Stays ASSUMED with the SEGLENGTH refusal named. Checked against the IMS 15.4 text copies

rules.title: EXEC DLI REPL / DLET USING PCB(n) SEGMENT(s) FROM(area) under CICS: the CBLTDLI REPL / DLET of the segment the previous get on this PCB held (DJ with none, DA for a changed key); SEGMENT must name the held segment's type; DIBSTAT the PCB's status
rules.ibm_note: IBM (IMS 15.4 Application Programming APIs, "REPL command"): "You must qualify the REPL command with at least one SEGMENT and FROM option, which together indicate the retrieved segments you want replaced"; "You cannot issue any commands using the same PCB between a Get command and the REPL command, and you can issue only one REPL command for each Get command"; "DLET command": "You must first retrieve segments you want to delete, just as if you were replacing segments. The DLET command deletes the retrieved segment and its dependents" (example: EXEC DLI GU SEGMENT(PATIENT) INTO(PATAREA), then EXEC DLI DLET SEGMENT(PATIENT) FROM(PATAREA)). The held segment, the PROCOPT A / R (REPL) check and the one-REPL-per-get rule MATCH. IBM does not say that SEGMENT must name the held segment's type: the runtime's refusal of a SEGMENT that does not is its own (stricter) check, so the rule stays ASSUMED. Checked against the IMS 15.4 text copies

rules.title: ISRT: the segment under the parent its SSAs (or current position) locate, among its twins by sequence field; II for a key its twins hold, GE for a parent not found; with command code D, a path insert from the root (each D-coded level kept or created from its slice of the I/O area); on a load-mode PCB (PROCOPT L / LS) the segment is appended in sequence, LB / LC / LD / LE for a duplicate, out-of-sequence, parentless or type-order violation
rules.ibm_note: IBM (IMS 15.4 Application Programming APIs, "ISRT call"; IMS 15.4 Messages and Codes Volume 4 (IMS Component Codes), II): "If the segment type you are inserting has a unique key field, the place where IMS adds the new segment occurrence depends on the value of its key field"; "The last SSA must be unqualified"; "If IMS returns a GE status code, at least one of the parents does not exist"; II "tried to insert a segment that already exists ... A segment with an equal physical twin sequence field already exists for the parent"; with D, "all the SSAs below and including the SSA containing the D command code" make a path insert. Those parts MATCH. Not matched to text: the FIRST / LAST / HERE rules for a non-unique or absent key (IBM: the DBD's RULES parameter; the runtime's reading of it is unchecked) and the load-mode codes LB / LC / LD / LE, which the text copy does not give. Stays ASSUMED (registers I1, I3). Checked against the IMS 15.4 text copies

rules.title: REPL / DLET on the segment the previous get-hold call returned; DJ without one, DA when the I/O area changed the sequence field; DLET removes the segment's dependents

CALL 'CBLTDLI' USING function pcb io-area [ssa ...]: the PCB the program was passed, the function's dispatch (AD for an unknown function, AM for one PROCOPT does not allow), any other DL/I call refused

A GSAM PCB in load mode: ISRT appends one record of the DBD's length to the output file, any other function is AM, and the PCB mask's segment level is blank; an SSA or an I/O area shorter than the record is refused
rules.ibm_note: IBM (IMS 15.4 Messages and Codes Volume 4 (IMS Component Codes), AM; IMS 15.4 Application Programming APIs, "ISRT call"; IMS 15.4 Application Programming, "PCB masks for GSAM databases"): AM "If the processing option is L and the program issued a call other than an ISRT call. Load programs can issue only ISRT calls." (the runtime's AM for any other function MATCHES). "When you use the ISRT call with GSAM, the area named by the i/o area parameter contains the record you want to add. The area must be long enough to hold these records" (an area shorter than the record refused is the caller's error). Open in IBM: the mask's segment level, "Segment Level Number. Not used by GSAM, but you must code it. It is 2 bytes", no value stated, so the runtime's blank is its own choice; the SSA refusal is not IBM text either. Stays ASSUMED (register I5). Checked against the IMS 15.4 text copies

rules.title: EXEC DLI SCHD PSB under CICS: the databases load at the first SCHD, the PSB's PCBs start with no position, DIBSTAT blank; a PSB already scheduled is TC (with NODHABEND), else refused; a planned TC (#5233) schedules the PSB first
rules.ibm_note: IBM (IMS 15.4 Messages and Codes Volume 4 (IMS Component Codes), TC; IMS 15.4 Application Programming APIs, "SCHD command", NODHABEND): TC "This status code applies to CICS online command-level programs only, and it is returned following a scheduling request. It means that you have already scheduled a PSB"; NODHABEND: a CICS transaction does not fail with a DHxx abend and, "Following an unsuccessful SCHD command, the control, as well as the status code in the DIB are passed back to the application program"; the codes not returned to the program abend, which fits refusing a SCHD of a scheduled PSB without NODHABEND. Those parts MATCH. Not in the text: that the databases load at the first SCHD and that the PCBs start with no position (IBM only says to "notify DL/I that your program will be accessing a database by scheduling a PSB"); DIBSTAT blank for success is what the manual's sample programs test ("CLC DIBSTAT,=C' '  IS STATUS BLANK"). Stays ASSUMED (register I5). Checked against the IMS 15.4 text copies

rules.title: EXEC DLI TERM: the scheduled PSB is released (the databases keep what was written), DIBSTAT blank; a TERM with no PSB scheduled is refused
rules.ibm_note: IBM (IMS 15.4 Application Programming APIs, "TERM command"): "The Terminate (TERM) command is used to terminate a PSB in a CICS online program." "If you want to use a PSB other than the one already scheduled, use the TERM command to release the PSB." "When you issue the TERM command, all database changes are committed and cannot be backed out." "No options are allowed with the TERM command. If your program subsequently needs a PSB that has terminated, it must reschedule that PSB by issuing another SCHD command." The runtime does this: the PSB is released and its PCBs dropped, what was written is kept (the committed changes), a later SCHD schedules again, DIBSTAT is blank (as for any success). The TERM call form adds "causes a CICS sync point"; the runtime refuses that call (RT-DLI-CALL) and takes no sync point for the EXEC form, whose text names only the database commit. IBM is silent on a TERM with no PSB scheduled, which the runtime refuses by name: a stated boundary, not a different answer. Stays ASSUMED only for that refusal and the sync point; the traced behaviour MATCHES (register I5). Checked against the IMS 15.4 text copies

rules.title: A planned DL/I fault (# DLI FUNCTION NTH|* STATUS; a get-hold counts as its get) replaces that call's execution, the PCB answering the status as for any status it names
rules.ibm_note: the faults are the harness's; the PCB feedback a fault leaves is assumed

rules.title: A COMP / COMP-4 / BINARY / COMP-5 item of 1-4 digits is a halfword, 5-9 a fullword, 10-18 a doubleword
A subscript is 1-based: offset + (index - 1) * the entry's length
Reference modification (start 1-based, no length: to the end) is an alphanumeric view of the item's bytes
A storage area (WORKING-STORAGE, LINKAGE, an FD record, a map) is its bytes; a DFHCOMMAREA of a stated EIBCALEN holds only those bytes, so a reference past them fails

ibm.section: EIB fields: EIBCALEN; LINK, COMMAREA and LENGTH

rules.ibm_note: IBM (CICS TS 6.x API Reference, EIB fields, EIBCALEN): "Contains the length of the communication area that has been passed to the application program from the last program, using the COMMAREA and LENGTH options. If no communication area is passed, this field contains binary zeros." EXEC CICS LINK: "When you use a COMMAREA to pass data, the program that is linked to must verify that the EIBCALEN field in the EIB of the task matches what the program expects. Discrepancies might result in storage violations or system failures." IBM so defines EIBCALEN as the passed length, and leaves a reference past it undefined (a storage violation or a failure, no stated result): the runtime's refusal past EIBCALEN is the harness's choice, register X23, so the rule stays ASSUMED. Checked against the CICS TS 6.x API Reference text copy

rules.title: Every byte value survives the record charset (a single-byte charset made lossless); X'hh..' is exactly its bytes
An ALPHABET (EBCDIC, or literals with ALSO and THRU): each data byte's position, the bytes no entry names after them in native order
A relation condition's nonnumeric operands under PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE: the shorter padded with spaces, then position by position in the alphabet
A key comparison IBM's EBCDIC sequence and the oracle's byte order decide differently, or one over a byte with no EBCDIC character, stops the run by name
SORT / MERGE keys compare as their items do in a relation condition (numeric by value, others byte by byte), the first the major key, ASCENDING / DESCENDING each
Equal keys come out in the order they went in (WITH DUPLICATES IN ORDER; the model keeps it always); MERGE: equal keys in the order the files are named
RELEASE / RETURN only inside the input / output procedure, USING files' records as they are, GIVING files each receiving every record; an implicit OPEN / READ / CLOSE that fails stops by name
SORT-RETURN written by the program: a 16 at a RELEASE / RETURN, or a value left in it when a sort ends, stops by name (IBM ends the sort at the 16 and resets the register to 0; GnuCOBOL does neither)
OPEN / CLOSE / READ / WRITE / REWRITE through CobolFiles, returning the FILE STATUS (the harness's planned statuses apply)
rules.ibm_note: IBM (Enterprise COBOL 6.4 Language Reference, File status key): "a value is placed in the specified file status key ... during execution of any request on that file; the value indicates the status of that request", placed before any EXCEPTION/ERROR declarative, INVALID KEY or AT END phrase runs; Table 34 gives the meanings. The code meanings are IBM's; that the oracle's files raise each code in the same situation as VSAM, and the order of checks when two apply, stay assumed. Declared in F1

rules.title: A keyed READ / WRITE / REWRITE: the record whose key bytes equal the record area's, found by the repository and verified against the key bytes
rules.ibm_note: IBM (Enterprise COBOL 6.4 Language Reference, READ statement, KEY IS phrase): "The KEY IS phrase can be specified only for indexed files. data-name-1 must identify a record key associated with file-name-1." IBM defines which key a keyed READ names, not how the record is found, so the repository lookup verified against the key bytes is the runtime's mechanism and stays assumed. Declared in F1

rules.title: A keyed file with no store bound: OPEN and CLOSE (their statuses) only; a record operation is a hole
rules.ibm_note: a record operation the translator could not bind is not modelled

rules.title: DISPLAY [WITH NO ADVANCING] to SYSOUT: the operands joined, in the record charset (a byte the charset leaves unmapped as its latin-1 byte), a record per DISPLAY
A user abend (CEE3ABD) carries its code, U followed by four digits

ibm.section: CEE3ABD: terminate enclave with an abend

rules.title: The task's queue manager: local queues, CCSID and messages from the case's mq.cfg; a name it does not hold is MQRC_UNKNOWN_OBJECT_NAME
rules.ibm_note: IBM documents 2085 for a name the queue manager cannot find; which queues exist, their CCSID and messages are the case's facts, not a z/OS queue manager's

rules.title: Only a CICS MQI call with Hconn MQHC_DEF_HCONN (0) is modelled; any other Hconn or MQI verb is refused by name
rules.ibm_note: the runtime stops by name outside the modelled calls

rules.title: MQOPEN: resolves the object descriptor, makes the object handle (1, 2, 3 ... in the order opened)
rules.ibm_note: IBM: the handle "ceases to be valid when the MQCLOSE call is issued" and is passed to later calls; its value is not defined, so the runtime's 1, 2, 3 numbering is the oracle's

rules.title: MQCLOSE: the handle becomes MQHO_UNUSABLE_HOBJ (-1)
rules.ibm_note: IBM sets Hobj to MQHO_UNUSABLE_HOBJ, but adds "On z/OS, Hobj is set to a value that is undefined"; the runtime's -1 is a choice where IBM leaves the z/OS value open (W4)

rules.title: MQGET (destructive): highest priority first, first in first out within it; WAIT on an empty queue ends at once with 2033, MQWI_UNLIMITED refused; MQGMO_CONVERT a no-op where the message is as asked, refused otherwise

ibm.section: MQGET: MQGMO_WAIT / WaitInterval, MQGMO_CONVERT; queue attribute MsgDeliverySequence

rules.ibm_note: priority-then-FIFO order matches MQMDS_PRIORITY; whether a queue is PRIORITY or FIFO by default is not in the text read (W3 contradicts itself); IBM waits the interval before 2033, the models answer at once on the no-producer assumption (W2)

rules.title: MQPUT / MQPUT1: MsgId GGMQ + a counter, the put context (PutApplType, PutDate / PutTime from the pinned clock, identity placeholders), the message queued under the unit of work
rules.ibm_note: IBM: a generated MsgId starts with a 4-byte product identifier (CSQ + blank on z/OS); the runtime's GGMQ + counter is the oracle's, declared in W4. The put-context fields match Table 529 (identity fields placeholders, W4)

rules.title: The MQ unit of work is the CICS task's: SYNCPOINT commits, SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK and an abend back out (BackoutCount raised), the task's end commits

ibm.section: Syncpoints in CICS Transaction Server for z/OS applications

rules.ibm_note: SYNCPOINT, SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK, the normal-end commit, the abnormal-end backout and BackoutCount are as IBM says; the z/OS cap of 255 on BackoutCount is not applied, and the joint syncpoint with ggcics.c is the oracle's (W5)

rules.title: SET ADDRESS OF a record TO a pointer into the PSA (a NULL pointer is address 0), the TCB (PSATNEW) or the TIOT (TCBTIO), and the pointer moved along its block through a numeric item it REDEFINES: the blocks laid from the stated job step at IBM's offsets; a record or an advance past what is laid is refused
A SYSIN deck read as commands (continuation, comments, SET MAXCC, IF/THEN/ELSE condition codes); a verb or operand the step does not model is refused by name
The command sequence run against the catalog: condition codes, the log, and IF tests of the last or maximum code
DELETE of a cluster, alternate index or path: a base takes its alternate indexes and paths with it only with CLUSTER named, otherwise refused
DEFINE CLUSTER, ALTERNATEINDEX and PATH: the entry, its keys and its record sizes; a name already cataloged or an unmodelled attribute is refused

ibm.section: DEFINE CLUSTER; DEFINE ALTERNATEINDEX; DEFINE PATH

rules.title: BLDINDEX builds an alternate index from its base: records ordered by alternate key, ties in primary-key order (checked against GnuCOBOL BDB alternate keys)
REPRO between sequential, ESDS, KSDS and a path: the record copy, the order of a KSDS, and a duplicate key refused
